root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Harrwitz Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bf4

overview: White develops the bishop to f4 before closing the c8-h3 diagonal, avoiding the Bg5 pin theory. Black replies with the standard QGD set-up of ...Be7, ...O-O and either ...c6 or the ...c5 break. White keeps tension, with e3, Nf3 and Bd3, and plays for a small space edge or a minority attack after cxd5.

white_ideas.idea: Develop the bishop actively to f4, then e3, Nf3, Qc2 and Bd3.
Pressure d5, possibly exchange on d5 and aim for a minority attack.

black_ideas.idea: Castle quickly and play ...c5 or ...c6 to free the position.
Meet cxd5 with ...exd5 and aim for easy piece play, or the Fianchetto Defense ...b6.

typical_structures.structure: QGD with tension on d5, either c6-Orthodox or ...c5 with an isolated d-pawn.
Carlsbad structure if White exchanges on d5.

character.notes: Standard QGD steadiness: Black's position is compact, and neither side has a forcing attack.

gambit.notes: Queen's Gambit declined, no material change.

structure.notes: Centre in tension; the QGD sits on Flexible.

approach.notes: Standard, a recognised sideline within the QGD.

level.notes: Familiar QGD plans; little forcing theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Fianchetto Defense
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Be7 4. Nf3 Nf6 5. Bf4 O-O 6. e3 b6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black fianchettos instead of playing ...c6; more flexible, with the long diagonal in play.

structure.reason: Centre stays in tension in the QGD.
